title: Tompkins County #1904: Flock termination notice deadline evidence boundary
summary: Narrows the County Flock exit timeline by separating the April 14 legislative termination resolution, a secondary transcript report of an April 28 written-notice deadline, the May 28 auto-renewal boundary, and still-unproved execution or technical offboarding.

evidence.claim: Tompkins County's own April 15 summary says the Legislature voted 12-1 on April 14 to terminate the County contract with Flock Group, Inc. before the May 28 auto-renewal.
A secondary meeting-summary transcript reports County Attorney Maury Josephson told the Legislature that written notice was required on or before April 28 to prevent an additional two-year renewal.

A contemporaneous report by Enfield Councilperson Robert Lynch describes the adopted resolution as directing the County Administrator and County Attorney to provide timely written termination notice to Flock before the auto-renewal date.

counterevidence: The County's own published highlights establish the May 28 auto-renewal boundary but do not themselves state the April 28 written-notice deadline.
The native adopted resolution, clerk-certified minutes, executed notice, vendor acknowledgment, and final contract closeout were not recovered in this pass.
gaps: Recover the native April 14 adopted resolution or certified meeting record containing the notice clause and deadline.
Recover proof that written termination notice was actually sent to and received by Flock by the required deadline.
Recover the exact contract-end state, final invoice/closeout, users/admins, credential revocations, SharedNetworks/audit exports, device disposition, and deletion/retention proof.

data.question: What does the April 14 record establish about the contractual written-notice deadline, and what remains unproved about execution and offboarding?
data.method: Deduped the current #1904 corpus first, rechecked Tompkins County's official April 14 summary and official meeting recording, then preserved the April 28 deadline only at secondary-transcript confidence pending recovery of the native adopted resolution/minutes.
data.framework: Legislative authorization, contractual notice deadline, notice transmission/receipt, auto-renewal avoidance, contract end, backend disablement, credential revocation, sharing removal, hardware removal, deletion, and billing closeout are separate predicates.
data.scope: Tompkins County Sheriff's Office Flock contract exit between the April 14, 2026 vote and May 28 auto-renewal boundary.
findings: Primary County evidence continues to establish a 12-1 April 14 vote to terminate before May 28.
The official County YouTube surface preserves the April 14 special meeting as a primary recording source.

A secondary transcript-derived summary reports an April 28 written-notice deadline to prevent a further two-year renewal; this is consistent with a notice period preceding the May 28 renewal point but is not promoted to primary-record status in this pass.
A contemporaneous local elected-official report independently describes the adopted resolution as directing timely written termination notice before auto-renewal.
No recovered evidence in this pass proves the notice was actually sent or received, the contract ended on a specific date, or technical/account/data offboarding completed.
conclusions: The legal lifecycle is now better bounded as April 14 authorization -> reported April 28 notice deadline -> May 28 auto-renewal boundary, while execution remains unresolved.
The April 28 deadline should remain a source-qualified fact until the native resolution or certified minutes are recovered.
No platform-state conclusion should be inferred from the legislative or contractual timeline alone.
recommendations: Recover the native April 14 adopted resolution and certified minutes from the County meeting portal.
Recover the executed termination notice, delivery/receipt evidence, vendor acknowledgment, and final invoice/closeout.
Then join those records to users/admins, credentials, SharedNetworks, audit exports, device disposition, retention/deletion, and billing state.
counterarguments: The County highlights use the May 28 auto-renewal boundary rather than publishing the reported April 28 notice deadline; the two dates describe different contract predicates and should not be collapsed.
A resolution directing notice is not proof notice was transmitted, accepted, or effective.
limitations: The meeting portal timed out during this pass, so the native resolution/minutes were not available for direct verification.
No private records, named search subjects, credentials, or unrelated personal information were collected.
unresolved: What is the resolution number and native adopted text?
Was termination notice sent and received on or before April 28, and through what delivery channel?
What exact date did the contract, accounts, sharing, devices, retained data, and billing relationship actually close?

data.research_question: Can the #1904 contract-exit timeline be narrowed beyond April 14 -> May 28 without overstating unverified termination execution?

classification_rules: Primary County evidence controls the April 14 vote and May 28 auto-renewal facts.
The April 28 written-notice deadline remains secondary-transcript evidence until the native resolution/minutes are recovered.
Direction to send notice is not proof of notice transmission or receipt.
Contract exit is not proof of technical/account/data offboarding.

findings.finding: The April 14 legislative action, reported April 28 notice deadline, and May 28 renewal boundary are separate contract states.
Executed notice and technical closeout remain unsupported by recovered evidence.
